conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 45 years old, male. I came in because I injured my ankle while playing basketball with my son. I landed awkwardly and twisted it, and now it's swollen, bruised, and really painful. It doesn't feel stable at all, and I'm having trouble walking on it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Could you please provide your age, gender, and a detailed description of your current symptoms, including when they started and any activities that worsen them?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I'm 45 years old, male. I injured my ankle while playing basketball with my son a few days ago. I landed awkwardly and twisted it, and now it's swollen, bruised, and really painful. It doesn't feel stable at all, and I'm having trouble walking on it. The pain is worse when I try to put weight on it, and it's been getting more swollen since the injury.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior ankle injuries or surgeries? Do you have a history of diabetes, hypertension, or any other chronic medical conditions?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: I don't have a history of ankle injuries or surgeries, and I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or hypertension. I've been pretty healthy overall.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you had any prior imaging, such as X-rays or an MRI, of the affected ankle since the injury?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: No, I haven't had any prior imaging of the affected ankle since the injury. This is the first time I'm seeing a doctor about it.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Can you describe the physical examination findings, including swelling, bruising, pain, instability, and any deformity? Also, please mention if there is any tenderness, range of motion, or crepitus, and whether you can bear weight on the ankle.

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: The doctor did a physical exam and found that my ankle is swollen on the outside, and there's a lot of tenderness, especially on the lateral side. When he pressed on the outside, it hurt pretty badly, and there was some tenderness on the inner part too. I can stand on it, but I can't walk on it because it feels unstable and hurts a lot. There's no obvious deformity, and my skin looks normal with good color and capillary refill.

conversation_turns.speaker: Doctor
conversation_turns.text: Have you undergone any imaging studies such as X-rays or MRI for the injured ankle?

conversation_turns.speaker: Patient
conversation_turns.text: Yes, I had an X-ray done when I came in today. The doctor showed me the results on the screen, and it looks like there's a fracture on the lateral side of my ankle. It's a displaced lateral malleolus at the Weber C level, and that's probably why it feels so unstable when I try to walk on it.
